name: Duke Energy
description: Duke Energy is a regulated electric and gas utility holding company. Its utilities (Duke Energy Carolinas, Progress, Florida, Ohio, Indiana and Kentucky) are the sole electricity supplier in their territories and serve about 8.7 million electric customers in six states over about 90,000 square miles, with about 55,713 MW of owned generation; its gas utilities (Piedmont and Ohio/Kentucky) serve about 1.8 million customers. State regulators set rates so the company can recover its costs plus a return on the capital it has invested (the rate base): allowed returns on equity in the filings are around 9.6% to 10.1% on equity ratios of roughly 51% to 53%. Earnings therefore grow mainly by investing more capital (over $1 billion a month per management commentary) and getting it approved in rate cases, not by selling more units in a competitive market.

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Utilities' and Sub-Industry 'Electric Utilities' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 4931 (Electric & Other Services Combined) per EDGAR.

hq.note: 525 South Tryon Street, Charlotte, NC 28202 (EDGAR business address)

employees.note: 26,441 full-time, part-time and temporary employees, of whom 5,027 are represented by unions (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (EU&I)
businessLines.how: Customers pay state-set tariffs each month for electricity; regulators allow the utility to recover operating costs and depreciation plus an allowed return on equity (about 9.6% to 10.1% in orders above) on the rate base, so profit grows as capital invested in plants and grid is added to rate base and approved in rate cases; fuel is passed through. In Ohio, only the delivery margin is earned, not the cost of the electricity.
businessLines.description: Regulated retail and wholesale electricity in the Carolinas, Florida and the Midwest (Ohio, Indiana, Kentucky): generation, transmission, distribution and sale to about 8.7 million customers.

businessLines.name: Gas Utilities and Infrastructure (GU&I)
businessLines.how: Customers pay regulated gas delivery rates each month (residential, commercial, industrial and power-generation); the utility earns a regulator-approved return on the pipes and storage it owns and passes through the cost of the gas itself (it earns margin on transmission and distribution 'and not on the cost of the underlying commodity').
businessLines.description: Piedmont Natural Gas (North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee; about 1.2 million customers), gas distribution in Ohio and Kentucky, plus gas storage, midstream pipeline and renewable natural gas investments. About 1.8 million customers in total, 1 million of them in the Carolinas.
